Hello to anyone who might be reading!

There was a small cheese community on the-site-that-shall-not-be-named, filled with mongers and people who just loved cheese. I'd love to get that kind of thing going here! I'm a former monger myself- spent 4.5 years in the business selling artisanal cheese, doing everything from working the line to inventory management to running our wholesale program. If anyone has any cheese- or pairing-related questions, I'll do my best to be checking back here frequently to answer them!

And just so there's something to discuss here- what is everyone's favorite cheese? Mine is Fourme d'Ambert (aged by Herve Mons). It's an ancient recipe that goes back something like 2000 years. The Romans wrote about this cheese. It's a raw, cow's milk Blue from the Auvergne region that tends to have a fudgey texture, decent salinity/minerality thanks to the blue veining, and a satisfying barnyardy/creamy flavor. I could eat that every day.

Looking forward to hearing from you!
I love cheese but I have never tried anything fancy. Is there anything good that might be available at a local grocer or deli that I should look for?
Probably a Manchego. It's a Spanish sheep's milk cheese. It's pretty common and very likeable. Not too funky but you can easily get it in 3 month, 6 month, and 1 year.

I don't know that there would be much I would consider "fancy" in the deli section, though I do love me some horseradish cheddar for sandwiches.

If there is a "specialty" cheese section there, give that a good look. People in the industry can tend to turn their noses up at things like Laughing Cow, but I don't think there's anything wrong with it. If it tastes good, then go for it.

What area are we talking about? What grocery stores are nearby?
I live in PA. There is a nearby Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, a place called Fresh Market, and a local chain called Giant Eagle.

Whole Foods should have a good selection.

Anything from The Cellars at Japser Hill will be well worth your investment- especially their Cabot Clothbound Cheddar (traditional, English-style cheddar) and Moses Sleeper (soft, buttery Camembert Style).

You should also be able to find some cheeses aged by a guy named Herve Mons. French styles. My favorites are Le Pommier Camembert (a traditional, French Camembert that's as close to the real deal as you can get here in the states), and his Fourme d'Ambert.

If you go at the right time, you should be able to just talk to the person working the counter and ask them what's good. That's the best way to make sure you're getting something tasty.

This is a great idea! I currently work in the specialty department at Whole Foods, I'm better versed in the beverages side but know a moderate amount about cheese and would love to learn more!

I love d'Ambert but Delice de Bourgogne has a special place in my heart. It's this super creamy triple cream brie that, when ripe, is more liquid than cheese. Simply amazing. There is another one at work that I fell in love with but the name escapes me. A french soft ripened cheese that goes well with jam? I'll make a point to look at it tomorrow.

Who doesn't love a good triple creme?

When it comes to soft-ripened cheeses, I tend to like mine on the milder/younger side. Moses Sleeper from Jasper Hill is one of my favorites- buttery, creamy, and kind of a peanut shell taste. Love it! Mt. Tam is a delicious triple creme from California that tends to be a bit firmer than Delice (which I quite enjoy!). But since Delice has to come over from France by boat, you tend to get something that's already nice and ripe and gooey.

Make sure you check on that cheese, I'd love to know what it is.
Freaking love Moses Sleeper! We sell Mt. Tam but I haven't had the opportunity to try it because we buy the little packaged balls so they don't need to be sliced.
It's definitely a very tasty cheese. Red Hawk, also from Cowgirl Creamery, is pretty decadent as well.

Pairing question, not sure if beer counts when discussing pairings, but here goes.

What is the best beer to go with a blue cheese burger? I usually have one with a Sam Adams and it is delicious, but I think I could do better.

Beer is my favorite thing, especially to go with cheese. With blues I tend to go with nice, big IPAs (or really any style with a crisp, hop-forward flavor profile). I feel like the nice, bitter flavors of IPAs or Pilsners is the perfect counter to a good juicy burger with some salty, funky blue cheese on top. I feel like maltier styles just wouldn't have the right "oomph" you need to be a standout accompaniment.

My old shop used to do a weekly beer pairing with a craft beer bar (which is my favorite place in the world; I moved away and really miss it). I've had lots of experience pairing beer and cheese, so if you have any more questions feel free to ask!

I'm excited I found this subverse!

My current cheese of choice is a La Tur which is a combo of cow, goat and sheep milk. The cheese guy at Whole Foods recommended it and I just love it!

Also, I've recently started making my own cheese. Just a simple farmer's cheese but I'm really enjoying that as well.
How did you get in the business of selling artisanal cheese if you don't mind me asking? I'm very interested.
